![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/6160de33d6b9e0cbd5cdfea19979a682398996f164e9654864ca8530d2048b51.png)

The Venn diagram above represents a universal set $S,$ two sets $A$ and $B,$ and the number of elements in each region of $S.$ An element from $A$ is selected at random. Calculate $P({B}^{′}|A).$
question.worked_solution:
To compute $P({B}^{′}|A),$ we need to ask, "what is the probability of $B$ *not* occurring given that $A$ has occurred?"

Since we are assuming that $A$ has occurred, we only consider the elements inside $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/cc16bfcd6588617a9181cb3798fbaba33a6cff3f1fb05b47d311d14bea3fb9f5.png)

In total, the number of elements inside $A$ is

$$
8+2=10.
$$

Of these $10$ elements, $8$ lie outside of $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273146/assets/4519280f1825097c175d9dd5636b3fb1cb59c5849b93fa07a6416056fa51b42f.png)

Since each outcome is equally likely, $P({B}^{′}|A)$ can be interpreted as the proportion of ${B}^{′}$ that lies inside $A,$ relative to the size of $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P({B}^{′}|A) & =\frac{8}{10}=\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
